subject: history_social
passage: Between roughly 1300 and 1850, average temperatures in the Northern Hemisphere fell in a period known as the Little Ice Age. Its coldest decades, in the seventeenth century, brought shortened growing seasons, repeated harvest failures, and hunger across much of Europe. Historian Tomasz Wieczorek argues that the wave of revolts and wars that historians call the crisis of the seventeenth century cannot be understood apart from this climate.
passage_b: The Dutch Republic reached the height of its wealth and power in exactly the decades Wieczorek describes. Historian Ingeborg Nystrand argues that the cold, far from harming the Dutch, worked in their favor: shifts in prevailing winds sped their ships to Asia, herring moved south into waters their fleets controlled, and their grain stores and canal networks let them profit from scarcity elsewhere. Climate shaped the century, Nystrand concludes, but what it did to any society depended on how that society was organized.
stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.A: The Dutch suffered more than other peoples during the Little Ice Age.
choices.B: Changes in prevailing winds were the main cause of harvest failures.
choices.C: Cold weather harmed every European society during the seventeenth century.
choices.D: The cooler climate of the seventeenth century affected European societies.

explanation.why: Wieczorek says the century's upheavals "cannot be understood apart from this climate." Nystrand says the cold "worked in their favor" for the Dutch and that "climate shaped the century." Both authors accept that the cooler climate had real effects on European societies; they differ over whether those effects were uniformly harmful.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nystrand says the Dutch reached the height of their wealth and that the cold worked in their favor.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 1 links harvest failures to shortened growing seasons; Text 2 mentions winds only as a benefit to Dutch shipping.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nystrand argues that the cold benefited the Dutch, so she would reject "every."
explanation.D: Correct. Both authors treat the climate as a force that shaped seventeenth-century societies.
